candidates.title: Positive Airway Pressure (PAP) Devices for the Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea

selection_reason: L33718 (PAP Devices for OSA) is the LCD governing E0601 CPAP coverage. The patient has OSA with documented CPAP intolerance despite mask refitting and pressure adjustment (6 of 30 nights, 1.5 h average), which fits the E0601 criteria of an in-person evaluation and sleep test. The order, however, is for a hypoglossal nerve stimulator implant, not a CPAP device, so L33718 is the PAP-device policy that applies to the E0601 code in the order. The other candidates address polysomnography and sleep testing, not PAP device coverage.

criteria.policy_text: The beneficiary has an in-person clinical evaluation by the treating practitioner prior to the sleep test to assess the beneficiary for obstructive sleep apnea.
criteria.explanation: The sleep test was done on 2026-10-02 (R45). The record window covers 2027-05-22 to 2029-05-22, and the only sleep medicine evaluation in the record (R36, R45) is dated 2029-03-31, after the sleep test. No in-person evaluation before 2026-10-02 is documented, so this criterion cannot be confirmed.

criteria.policy_text: The beneficiary has a sleep test (as defined below) that meets either of the following criteria (1 or 2): 1. The apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) or Respiratory Disturbance Index (RDI) is greater than or equal to 15 events per hour with a minimum of 30 events; or, 2. The AHI or RDI is greater than or equal to 5 and less than or equal to 14 events per hour with a minimum of 10 events and documentation of: a. Excessive daytime sleepiness, impaired cognition, mood disorders, or insomnia; or, b. Hypertension, ischemic heart disease, or history of stroke.
criteria.explanation: Alternative 1 applies. The diagnostic polysomnogram recorded an AHI of 32 events per hour, with 189 events over 5.9 hours of sleep (R45). That is at or above 15 per hour, and the 189 events exceed the minimum of 30. The record does not indicate PAP use during that study. The OSA diagnosis is recorded in R28.

criteria.policy_text: The beneficiary and/or their caregiver has received instruction from the supplier of the device in the proper use and care of the equipment.
criteria.explanation: R34 shows a home CPAP unit and R40 and R42 show device downloads, so the patient has used a CPAP device. Nothing in the record documents that the supplier gave instruction in proper use and care of the equipment, so this cannot be confirmed.

criteria.policy_text: A sleep test (Type I, II, III, IV, Other) that meets the Medicare requirements for a valid sleep test as outlined in NCD 240.4.1 and the applicable A/B MAC LCD and Billing and Coding article.
criteria.explanation: The diagnostic study is named as an attended polysomnography (R45). The policy defines a polysomnogram performed in a facility-based laboratory as a Type I study, so the test type is named and qualifies. The remaining validity requirements are administrative and were not assessed.

criteria.policy_text: The sleep test results meet the coverage criteria in effect for the date of service of the claim for the PAP device.
criteria.explanation: The AHI of 32 events per hour with 189 events over 5.9 hours meets the AHI threshold of at least 15 per hour with at least 30 events under the diagnostic criteria (see I.B).

criteria.policy_text: The sleep test is ordered by the beneficiary's treating practitioner.
criteria.explanation: The record says the diagnosis was made by attended polysomnography on 2026-10-02 but does not say who ordered that test. The ordering practitioner is not documented, so this cannot be confirmed.

decision_explanation: The diagnostic sleep study meets the AHI threshold (I.B, Sleep Tests.1, Sleep Tests.3), but three applicable criteria are not documented: the pre-sleep-test in-person evaluation (I.A), supplier instruction in equipment use (I.C), and the treating practitioner's order for the sleep test (Sleep Tests.4). No criterion is contradicted by the record. The continued-coverage adherence data (R40, R42) and the later-therapy requirements were not assessed because they concern a later stage of therapy and do not apply to initial coverage. Administrative requirements (FDA status, provider qualification, SWO, proof of delivery) were excluded.
